current_activity: Relieves 3rd Division in the line east of the Falaise road at 04:30, in the area Four-Bourguebus
notes: Event date: 31 July 1944, 04:30 (Stacey, p. 202). Event definition: Maj.-Gen. Kitching 4th Armoured Division, the last Canadian division to reach the theatre, enters the line under II Canadian Corps and relieves the 3rd Division, the relief being completed at 04:30; it now confronts the enemy immediately east of the great road to Falaise in the area Four-Bourguebus. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 202: "entered the line under the 2nd Canadian Corps at the end of July"; "The relief was completed at 4:30 a.m. on 31 July"; "The 4th Division now confronted the enemy immediately east of the great road to Falaise". Location: Bourguebus area, Calvados with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is Bourguebus and stands for the sector given by Stacey as the area Four-Bourguebus. Location support: Stacey gives the area Four-Bourguebus, east of the road to Falaise (p. 202). Commander: Maj.-Gen. G. Kitching (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 1 Mar. 44 to 21 Aug. 44).

current_activity: Totalize phase II: Argylls and South Alberta Regiment take Cintheaux about 18:00 and push on to Hautmesnil
notes: Event date: 8 August 1944, about 18:00 (Stacey, p. 224). Event definition: In the second phase of Operation Totalize the 4th Armoured Division crosses the lateral road Bretteville-sur-Laize to St. Aignan de Cramesnil at 13:55; about 18:00 The Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders of Canada and the South Alberta Regiment take Cintheaux and two companies of the Argylls capture Hautmesnil, the farthest limit of the division advance that day. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 224: "The Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders of Canada and the South Alberta Regiment took Cintheaux"; "This was the farthest limit of the 4th Division's penetration that day". Location: Cintheaux, Calvados with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey names Cintheaux and Hautmesnil (p. 224). Commander: Maj.-Gen. G. Kitching (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 1 Mar. 44 to 21 Aug. 44).

current_activity: Tractable: tanks cross the Laison at Ernes, Rouvres and Maizieres; 10th Brigade takes Olendon in the evening
notes: Event date: 14 August 1944 (Stacey, p. 241). Event definition: On the first day of Operation Tractable the tanks of the 4th Armoured Division cross the Laison at Ernes, Rouvres and Maizieres, and shortly before midnight the armoured regiments of the 4th Armoured Brigade are disposed about Olendon, which the 10th Infantry Brigade has captured in the evening. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 241: "On the 4th Division front, some tanks, seeking a crossing"; "the armoured regiments of the 4th Armoured Brigade were disposed about Olendon". Location: Olendon, Calvados with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey names Olendon, Ernes, Rouvres and Maizieres (p. 241). Commander: Maj.-Gen. G. Kitching (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 1 Mar. 44 to 21 Aug. 44).

current_activity: Ordered to seize a crossing over the Ante at Damblainville and advance on Trun
notes: Event date: 16 August 1944, morning (Stacey, p. 250). Event definition: The division, which had been planning another attack on the high ground north of Falaise, is told on the morning of 16 August to move instead to seize a crossing over the Ante River in the Damblainville area and advance south-east along the main highway to Trun, to close the gap between First Canadian and Third United States Armies. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 250: "which had been planning another attack on the high ground north of Falaise"; "in the Damblainville area and advance along the axis of the main highway running south-east to". Location: Damblainville, Calvados with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the page gives the order, not the position reached; the point is the objective area. Location support: Stacey gives the Damblainville area as the objective of the division (p. 250). Commander: Maj.-Gen. G. Kitching (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 1 Mar. 44 to 21 Aug. 44).

current_activity: Trun occupied by the 10th Brigade as the armour pushes on to close the Falaise Gap
notes: Event date: 18 August 1944 (Stacey, p. 256; CMH, Breakout and Pursuit, p. 532). Event definition: The 4th Armoured Division pushes south-east to close the Gap: the enemy does not try to hold Trun, which the 10th Infantry Brigade occupies during the day, and the 4th Armoured Brigade pushes across the Trun-Vimoutiers road. Event support: two source families (Stacey, the Canadian official history; the US Army Center of Military History, Breakout and Pursuit) (the CMH text on p. 532 says the 4th Canadian Armoured Division took Trun on 18 August). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 256: "The enemy was apparently not attempting to hold the town, which was occupied by the 10th Infantry Brigade during the day". Location: Trun, Orne with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey and the US Army official history both name the town of Trun. Commander: Maj.-Gen. G. Kitching (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 1 Mar. 44 to 21 Aug. 44).

current_activity: Argylls and South Alberta Regiment fight for St. Lambert-sur-Dives and get halfway through it
notes: Event date: 19 August 1944 (Stacey, p. 260). Event definition: In the morning B Company of The Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders of Canada and C Squadron of The South Alberta Regiment under Major Currie attack St. Lambert and after six hours of fighting get halfway through the village; reinforced in the afternoon by a company of the Argylls and one of The Lincoln and Welland Regiment, the force can make no further progress and digs in. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 260: "During the 19th there was a desperate struggle at St. Lambert"; "attacked the village and after six hours". Location: St. Lambert-sur-Dives, Calvados (existing place PL0511) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey names the village of St. Lambert (p. 260). Commander: Maj.-Gen. G. Kitching (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 1 Mar. 44 to 21 Aug. 44).

current_activity: Lincoln and Welland cross the Seine near Criquebeuf at 17:00; division is to seize a bridgehead there
notes: Event date: 26 August 1944, 17:00 (Stacey, pp. 283 and 287). Event definition: By Simonds orders the 4th Division is to seize by coup-de-main a bridgehead beyond the Seine in the area of Pont de l Arche and Criquebeuf; at 17:00 on 26 August the scout platoon and D Company of The Lincoln and Welland Regiment cross the river near Criquebeuf, above Elbeuf, in a small boat, the first Canadians across the Seine. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 283: "crossed the Seine near Criquebeuf, above Elbeuf"; p. 287: "They required the 4th Division to seize". Location: Criquebeuf-sur-Seine, Eure with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey names Criquebeuf (pp. 283 and 287). Commander: Maj.-Gen. H. W. Foster (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 22 Aug. 44 to 30 Nov. 44).

current_activity: Passes under I Corps at midnight 17-18 October after concentrating north-east of Antwerp
notes: Event date: 17-18 October 1944, midnight (Stacey, p. 390). Event definition: The division completes its concentration north-east of Antwerp on 17 October and comes under I Corps (Stacey: 1st Corps) at midnight, to carry out the operation later named Suitcase, on the left of the 49th Division and directed on Esschen. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 390: "On 17 October the 4th Division completed its"; "concentration north-east of Antwerp. It came under the 1st Corps at midnight". Location: Antwerp area (north-east of the city), Belgium (existing place PL0574) with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: the point is the city of Antwerp, standing for a concentration area north-east of it, with a wide precision. Location support: Stacey gives the concentration area north-east of Antwerp (p. 390). Commander: Maj.-Gen. H. W. Foster (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 22 Aug. 44 to 30 Nov. 44).

current_activity: Operation Suitcase: division launched at 07:30 towards Esschen, with Bergen op Zoom beyond
notes: Event date: 20 October 1944, 07:30 (Stacey, p. 390). Event definition: At 07:30 on a wet and chilly morning General Foster launches the division towards Esschen, with Bergen op Zoom as a further objective, to clear the flank of the 2nd Division; the 49th Division attacks on the axis Brecht-Wuestwezel on its right. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 390: "the 4th Canadian Armoured Division on its left directed on Esschen"; "General Foster launched his division towards Esschen". Location: Essen (Esschen), Antwerp province, Belgium with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Stacey names Esschen as the objective (p. 390). Commander: Maj.-Gen. H. W. Foster (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 22 Aug. 44 to 30 Nov. 44).

current_activity: 10th Brigade occupies Steenbergen after fighting at Welberg; the last mainland corner south of the Maas
notes: Event date: 4 November 1944 (Stacey, p. 424). Event definition: Fighting north from Bergen op Zoom in the last corner of the mainland below the Maas, the 4th Armoured Brigade is checked at Welberg on the night of 31 October-1 November, the 10th Infantry Brigade takes over and clears Welberg on the night of 2-3 November, and on 4 November it occupies Steenbergen. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 424: "the 4th Canadian Armoured Division, fighting north from Bergen op Zoom"; "on 4 November the 10th Brigade occupied Steenbergen". Location: Steenbergen, Noord-Brabant with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Stacey names Steenbergen (p. 424). Commander: Maj.-Gen. H. W. Foster (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: 22 Aug. 44 to 30 Nov. 44).

current_activity: Relieved by the Poles on 21 December; in Army Reserve in the Boxtel area on six hours notice to move
notes: Event date: after 21 December 1944, the day of the relief by the Poles (Stacey, p. 443); the claim date 23 December is representative. Event definition: General Vokes 4th Armoured Division, relieved by the Poles on 21 December, is placed in Army Reserve in the Boxtel area on six hours notice to move; the claim is dated 23 December as a representative date within the Christmas precautions, the exact date of the placing in reserve not being given. Event support: one source family (Stacey, the Canadian official history). Stacey, The Victory Campaign, p. 443: "which had been relieved by the Poles on the 21st, was placed in Army Reserve in the Boxtel area, on six hours"; "notice to move". Location: Boxtel area, Noord-Brabant with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: Stacey gives the area; the point is the town of Boxtel. Location support: Stacey names the Boxtel area (p. 443). Commander: Maj.-Gen. C. Vokes (Stacey, Appendix G, p. 666: from 1 Dec. 44).
